_about: THE ACTION CONTRACT, as the browser sees it. Day 14b.
Why this file exists. The GenAI boundary has had two conformance tests since Day 14 —
one against /openapi.json and one against GET /tools — so Python and Java cannot drift
without a build failing. The BROWSER boundary had none. Type.ts was hand-written
against Spring's DTOs and checked by nobody, which is two of the four copies the
Month 2 drift came from.
It is asserted from BOTH SIDES against the same bytes:
backend   ActionContractSnapshotTest reflects over the enums and payload records
frontend  src/Type.conformance.test.ts reads an identical copy at src/test/
So this snapshot cannot be edited to make either side pass: changing it to suit the
frontend breaks the Java test, and changing Java breaks this snapshot until it is
regenerated, at which point the frontend test fails until Type.ts follows. That is the
property a comment saying 'keep these in sync' never had.
WHAT IT FOUND IMMEDIATELY, before it had ever guarded anything:
* ActionService returned the summary as a BARE STRING while ActionCard.tsx renders
result.summary — so an approved summary rendered as an empty card, no error.
* Type.ts exported `ActionStatus = 'pending' | 'approved' | 'rejected'`, which
matches no backend enum at all. It had zero consumers, which is why nothing broke.
Spelling note. Keys here are the WIRE spelling the browser receives — camelCase for
Spring's payloads, hyphens for the discriminator values. GET /tools publishes Python's
snake_case for the same tools and that is not a contradiction: Python's schema is what
a MODEL may produce, this is what a BROWSER receives, and ActionProposer is the
translation between them. ToolRegistryConformanceTest asserts that bridge.
